2024_002_8_a_troy_sd_2024_operating_mill.paragraph: Non-homestead operating tax millage analysis prepared for the Troy School District by PFM Financial Advisors LLC and dated February 20, 2024, presented as item 8.A. at the March 19, 2024 Board meeting. It documents twenty years of operating millage history drawn from Oakland Equalization Department records and District L-4029 forms, and models the state aid the District would forgo under continued Headlee millage reduction fraction rollbacks. At a 4-mill buffer with a 0.9882 rollback factor, the projected cumulative loss over the 2026 through 2045 levy years is $5,902,057.

**Author and date**
PFM Financial Advisors LLC, 555 Briarwood Circle, Suite 333, Ann Arbor, Michigan 48108, office 734-994-9700, Pfm.com. Titled "Troy School District Non Homestead Operating Tax Millage Rate," dated February 20, 2024. Source noted as the Oakland Equalization Department and School District historical L-4029 forms.

**Historical operating millage**
Each levy year shows operating millage levied, hedge millage levied, total operating levy and the millage reduction fraction (MRF).

| 2022 | 16.9612 | 1.0388 | 18.0000 | 0.9693 |

| 2020 | 17.6413 | 0.3587 | 18.0000 | 0.9954 |
| 2019 | 17.7228 | 0.2772 | 18.0000 | 0.9846 |
| 2018 | 18.0000 | 0.0000 | 18.0000 | 1.0000 |

Levy years 2013 through 2004 each show 18.0000 mills levied with no hedge millage and an MRF of 1.0000. Averaged reduction fractions are stated as 0.9882 (5-year), 0.9916 (10-year), 0.9944 (15-year) and 0.9958 (20-year).

**Estimated loss in annual state aid funding**
Three scenarios are modeled over twenty levy years beginning 2026: a 4.0000 mill buffer at a 0.9900 rollback, a 4.0000 mill buffer at 0.9882, and a 5.0000 mill buffer at 0.9882. All three show $0 in levy years 1 through 15 (2026 through 2040).

| Levy Year | 4.0000 Mill / 0.9900 | 4.0000 Mill / 0.9882 | 5.0000 Mill / 0.9882 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 16 – 2041 | 0 | 51,133 | 0 |
| 17 – 2042 | 0 | 600,253 | 0 |
| 18 – 2043 | 0 | 1,164,721 | 0 |
| 19 – 2044 | 16,254 | 1,744,877 | 0 |
| 20 – 2045 | 509,886 | 2,341,072 | 204,424 |
| Total | $526,140 | $5,902,057 | $204,424 |

**Assumptions**
Estimated 2023 equivalent Non-PRE taxable value of $1,722,654,355; annual growth in Non-PRE taxable value of 5% in 2024 and 2% thereafter; constant Headlee rollback millage reduction fractions as noted, with actual MRF expected to vary each year; the tables exclude any effect on the Hold Harmless millage and are described as for informational purposes only.

**Detailed calculation, 4-mill buffer at 0.9882**
The year-by-year schedule starts from $1,722,654,355 of non-homestead taxable value in 2023 at 18.0000 mills, grows the base to 1,808,787,073 in 2024 and 1,844,962,814 in 2025, and continues at 2% growth to 2,741,517,691 by 2045. The maximum allowable rate erodes from 18.0000 to 14.0286 mills and the buffer from 4.0000 to 3.1175 mills; the combined levy stays at 18.0000 mills through 2040, then falls to 17.9798 in 2041, 17.7676 in 2042, 17.5580 in 2043, 17.3508 in 2044 and 17.1461 in 2045, generating the revenue losses that cumulate to $5,902,057.

2024_008_resolution_certifying_ballot_la.paragraph: Resolution of the Troy School District Board of Education, County of Oakland, State of Michigan, adopted at a special meeting held June 6, 2024 at 5 p.m., certifying an Operating Millage Renewal Proposal to the Oakland County Clerk for the November 5, 2024 election. The ballot language asks electors to increase the taxing limitation by 22 mills, with 18 mills the maximum allowable levy, for twenty years covering 2026 through 2045, with no more than 5.7049 mills on principal residences. The proposal is estimated to produce $42.5 million during the 2026 calendar year.
2024_008_resolution_certifying_ballot_la.page:
**Meeting and form**
Minutes of a special meeting of the Board of Education of the Troy School District, County of Oakland, State of Michigan, held in the School District on June 6, 2024 at 5 p.m. local time. Present and absent member lines, the mover and supporter names, and the YES and NO tallies are left blank in this packet copy. Gary Hauff signs as Secretary, Board of Education, both on the resolution and on the certification that the copy is true and complete and that the meeting complied with the Open Meetings Act, Act 267, Public Acts of Michigan, 1976.

**Purpose**
The preamble states the Board has determined it necessary for continued operation to renew the authority to levy certain operating mills and to increase the prior authority to protect against the impact of future rollbacks under the Headlee Amendment, as described in the Operating Millage Renewal Proposal attached as Exhibit A.

**Certification deadlines**
The Proposal must be certified to the Clerk of the County of Oakland, acting as School District Election Coordinator, no later than 4:00 p.m. on August 13, 2024, in order to appear on the November 5, 2024 election. The Secretary of the Board and the Superintendent are each individually authorized to file the resolution and complete required forms by that deadline, and are further authorized to update the Proposal before submission to reflect any Headlee rollbacks applicable to the current operating millage for the 2024 year. The Election Coordinator is directed to post and publish notice of the last day of registration and notice of election, and to have ballots prepared and printed in the Exhibit A form. Conflicting resolutions are rescinded.

**Exhibit A – Operating Millage Renewal Proposal**
The explanatory paragraph states the proposal would renew authority that expires with the 2025 tax levy to levy up to 18.00 mills for general school district operating purposes on non-exempt taxable property, restrict the levy on principal residences to no more than 5.7049 mills, and protect against Headlee rollbacks of up to 4.0 mills. It notes the District levied only 2.7936 mills on principal residences in 2024, and that non-homestead property is principally industrial and commercial real property and residential rental property.

**Ballot question**

| Element | Value |
|---|---|
| Increase in limitation | 22 mills |
| Maximum allowable levy | 18 mills ($18.00 per $1,000 of taxable value) |
| Cap on principal residences | 5.7049 mills |
| Term | twenty (20) years, 2026 to 2045 inclusive |
| Estimated revenue, calendar 2026 | $42.5 million |

The ballot closes with YES and NO options.
2024_008_resolution_certifying_ballot_la.verbose:
Resolution Certifying Operating Millage Renewal Proposal, prepared as minutes of a special meeting of the Board of Education of the Troy School District, County of Oakland, State of Michigan, held in the School District on June 6, 2024 at 5 p.m. local time. The document is formatted with blank lines for members present, members absent, the offering member, the supporting member, and the YES and NO votes; the packet copy is therefore unexecuted as to names and tallies.

PREAMBLE. The first whereas clause records that the Board has determined it is necessary for the continued operation of the School District to renew the authority to levy certain operating mills and to increase the prior authority in order to protect against the impact of future rollbacks under the Headlee Amendment, as described in the Operating Millage Renewal Proposal attached as Exhibit A. The second whereas clause states it is necessary and desirable to submit the Proposal to the School District's electors at an election to be held on November 5, 2024, defined as the November Election Date. The third whereas clause states that in order for the Proposal to be submitted on that date, the Board must certify the Proposal to the Clerk of the County of Oakland, State of Michigan, defined as the School District Election Coordinator, as required by the Michigan election laws, not later than 4:00 p.m. on August 13, 2024.

RESOLVED CLAUSES. Paragraph 1 certifies the Exhibit A Proposal to the School District Election Coordinator and the local clerks for submission to the electors on the November Election Date, and individually authorizes and directs the Secretary of the Board and the Superintendent to file the Resolution and complete any forms, certificates or documents required by the Election Coordinator and local clerks to evidence the certification and submission by no later than 4:00 p.m. on August 13, 2024. Paragraph 2 further authorizes the Secretary of the Board or the Superintendent, prior to submission, to update the Proposal to reflect any Headlee rollbacks applicable to the current operating millage for the 2024 year. Paragraph 3 authorizes and directs the School District Election Coordinator to post and publish notice of the last day of registration and notice of election for the November Election Date, and to have prepared and printed ballots for submitting the Proposal in the form appearing in Exhibit A, or to state the proposition as a proposal on the voting machines, permitting the ballots to include other matters presented to the electorate on the same date. Paragraph 4 rescinds all resolutions and parts of resolutions insofar as they conflict with this Resolution. The resolution is declared adopted.

SIGNATURES AND CERTIFICATION. Gary Hauff signs as Secretary, Board of Education. A separate certification block, also signed by Gary Hauff as Secretary, certifies that the foregoing is a true and complete copy of a resolution adopted by the Board of Education of the Troy School District, County of Oakland, State of Michigan at a special meeting held on June 6, 2024, that the meeting was conducted and public notice given pursuant to and in full compliance with the Open Meetings Act, being Act 267, Public Acts of Michigan, 1976, and that minutes of the meeting were kept and will be or have been made available as required by that Act.

EXHIBIT A – OPERATING MILLAGE RENEWAL PROPOSAL. The explanatory text states that the proposal would renew the authority of the School District, which expires with the 2025 tax levy, to levy up to 18.00 mills for general school district operating purposes on taxable property in the School District to the extent that such property is not exempt from such levy; restrict the levy on principal residences, meaning owner-occupied homes, to no more than 5.7049 mills; and protect against the impact of Headlee rollbacks of up to 4.0 mills. The authorization would allow the School District to continue to levy the statutory limit of 18.00 mills on non-homestead property, described as principally industrial and commercial real property and residential rental property, and to continue to levy on principal residence property only that portion of the mills necessary to allow the School District to receive the full revenue per pupil foundation allowance permitted by the State. The text records that the School District only levied 2.7936 mills on personal residences, that is owner-occupied homes, in 2024.

BALLOT QUESTION. The question asks whether the limitation on the amount of taxes which may be imposed on taxable property in the Troy School District, County of Oakland, Michigan, shall be increased in the amount of 22 mills, with 18 mills being the maximum allowable levy at $18.00 per $1,000 of taxable value, to the extent such property is not statutorily exempt, and of which not more than 5.7049 mills may be imposed on principal residences, for twenty (20) years covering the years 2026 to 2045 inclusive, to provide funds for operating expenses of the School District. The question states that the operating millage, if approved and levied, would provide estimated revenues to the School District of $42.5 million during the 2026 calendar year, to be used for general operating purposes. The ballot presents YES and NO choices.

The structure of the request pairs an 18-mill operating levy with a 4-mill Headlee buffer above it, matching the modeling PFM Financial Advisors LLC presented to the Board in February 2024, and the 5.7049-mill principal residence cap preserves the hold harmless component of the District's homestead levy.

2024_009_24_25mhsaaresolution.page:
**What the document is**
The annual Michigan High School Athletic Association membership resolution, a fill-in form that a Board of Education must formally ratify and sign to obtain or continue MHSAA membership. The MHSAA address is 1661 Ramblewood Drive, East Lansing, MI 48823, telephone (517) 332-5046. Completed forms are to be saved and emailed as an attachment to camala@mhsaa.com. One signed copy is returned to the MHSAA and one retained by the district.

**Membership terms**
The MHSAA is described as a voluntary, nonprofit corporation of public, private and parochial junior high, middle and senior high schools whose boards have applied for and received membership. Member boards agree to abide by and enforce MHSAA rules, regulations and qualifications on eligibility, game rules and tournament policies, procedures and schedules. Participation in MHSAA postseason tournaments requires high schools to adhere to at least the minimum standards of Regulation I and the maximum limitations of Regulation II in all MHSAA tournament sports. MHSAA tournaments are stated to be the collective property of the MHSAA rather than any individual member school, with the association reserving publication, exclusivity, anti-commercialization and image or transmission rights. Resolutions that are modified or supplemented with conditional letters are rejected.

**Resolution text**
The resolution enrolls the named schools as members of the Michigan High School Athletic Association, Inc. and further enrolls them to participate in approved interschool athletic activities. The Board delegates to the Superintendent or designee the responsibility for supervision and control of those activities, accepts the association's Constitution and By-Laws, and adopts its rules, regulations and interpretations as published in the current Handbook as minimum standards and the governing code, agreeing to primary enforcement. The authorization runs from August 1, 2024 to July 31, 2025 and may not be revoked during that period. A Record of Adoption block provides for the school name, the day and month in 2024, the governing body name, address, city and zip, contact e-mail, and the Board Secretary or designee signature.

**Membership eligibility rules**
Membership requires a school building with enrollment and onsite attendance of at least 15 students, for grades 6 through 8 or 9, 7 through 8 or 9, or 9 or 10 through 12; nonpublic schools must qualify for federal income tax exemption as a not-for-profit organization. Schools may join at the sixth-grade level to reach the 15-student minimum whether or not sixth graders participate in athletics. Section A states the rules do not require districts to become members at the junior high or middle school level, nor to sponsor interscholastic athletics for sixth graders. Section B states that if a listed junior high or middle school sponsors a sixth-grade team in any sport or permits a sixth grader to participate with seventh and eighth graders, all of Regulations III and IV apply to all sixth graders in all sports involving sixth graders on that school's teams; if no sixth graders participate in a sport, MHSAA rules do not apply in that sport.

| Smith Middle School | 6-8 | 6, 7, 8 marked |

Michigan High School Athletic Association membership resolution form for the 2024-25 school year, included in the Troy School District Board of Education packet for the meeting of June 20, 2024. The MHSAA's address on the form is 1661 Ramblewood Drive, East Lansing, MI 48823, with telephone (517) 332-5046, and completed forms are to be saved and sent as an attachment to camala@mhsaa.com.

ORGANIZATIONAL DESCRIPTION. The form describes the Michigan High School Athletic Association as a voluntary, nonprofit corporation comprised of public, private and parochial junior high, middle and senior high schools whose Boards of Education or Governing Bodies have voluntarily applied for and received membership for and on behalf of their secondary schools. The association sponsors statewide tournaments and makes eligibility rules with respect to participation in MHSAA-sponsored tournaments in the various sports. Each Board of Education or Governing Body that wishes to host or participate in such meets and tournaments must join the MHSAA and agree to abide by and enforce the MHSAA rules, regulations and qualifications concerning eligibility, game rules and tournament policies, procedures and schedules. It is a condition of participation in any MHSAA postseason tournament that high schools adhere to at least the minimum standards of Regulation I and the maximum limitations of Regulation II in all MHSAA tournament sports.

PROPRIETARY RIGHTS. The form states that MHSAA tournaments are the collective property of the MHSAA and not of any individual member school, and that the MHSAA reserves the right to promote and advance the membership's interests with publication information; exclusive arrangements to create recognition and exposure for school-sponsored activities; restrictive policies prohibiting exploitation and commercialization of MHSAA-sponsored tournaments; appropriate proprietary interests; and the use of images or transmissions identifying contest officials, spectators and member schools' students, personnel and marks.

ADOPTION MECHANICS. To obtain membership, the Board of Education or Governing Body must adopt the resolution for its junior high, middle and senior high schools. Pursuant to the MHSAA Constitution, all high schools, junior high or middle schools, or other schools of Michigan doing a corresponding grade of work may become members provided (a) the school building has enrollment and onsite attendance of at least 15 students, whether for grades 6 through 8 or 9, grades 7 through 8 or 9, or grades 9 or 10 through 12; and (b) if a nonpublic school, the school qualifies for federal income tax exemption as a not-for-profit organization. To reach the 15-student minimum for middle school membership, schools may join the MHSAA at the sixth-grade level whether or not sixth-grade students participate in athletics. Paragraph A states that the section does not require school districts to become member schools at the junior high or middle school level and does not require them to sponsor any interscholastic athletics for sixth-grade students. Paragraph B states that if a school district's MHSAA Membership Resolution lists a junior high or middle school as an MHSAA member school, and if the school sponsors a sixth-grade team in any sport or permits a sixth-grade student to participate with seventh- and eighth-grade students in any sport, then all of Regulations III and IV apply to all sixth-graders in all sports involving sixth-graders on teams sponsored by that school; if the school does not allow any sixth-graders to participate in a sport, MHSAA rules do not apply in that sport.
